decisions.decision: Monthly periods are the phasing granularity.
decisions.note: User chose monthly over the recommended quarterly. Consequence surfaced before the choice: 36 rows per initiative over a 3-year horizon. Accepted, mitigated by D-05 auto-fill.

decisions.decision: Track run-rate (steady-state annual) separately from in-year realized value.
decisions.note: Matches the distinction practitioners treat as essential — an initiative can be at 100% run-rate while in-year banked value is far lower.

decisions.decision: Phasing horizon is 3 years, configurable per deal.
decisions.note: Covers the standard cost-synergy ramp to full run-rate; configurable so a small acquisition is not forced into a full 3-year grid.

decisions.decision: Existing targetM / realizedM become DERIVED TOTALS (rollup of the phased rows), not removed and not independently editable.
decisions.note: Chosen for demo-showcase safety — every existing consumer (demo showcase, PMO console, dashboards) keeps working untouched. The demo is a maintained deliverable per PROJECT.md.

decisions.decision: Monthly rows are generated by ramp-template auto-fill: IL enters run-rate + start month + curve shape (cost 30/70/100, revenue 10/40/70, or linear), rows generate automatically and stay individually editable.
decisions.note: This is what makes monthly granularity workable. Curve shapes taken from standard PMI ramp practice.

decisions.decision: Realized value is editable ONLY for months that have arrived — no forward-booking of value into future months.
decisions.note: Credibility control: forward-booked value is the main way synergy tracking loses trust.

code_ground_truth.current_model: { id, title, category: 'cost'|'revenue', targetM, realizedM, owner, workstreamId, status, notes, createdAt }
code_ground_truth.deal_isolation_note: readDb/writeDb come from db/store.js and resolve to the bound deal's SQLite DB; both synergy collections are in ARRAY_COLLECTIONS (35 total). Verified 2026-08-03, correcting an initial mis-read that they lived in a shared db.json.
